G3517.name: Nereus
G3517.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3517.brief: A Christian in Rome greeted by Paul.
G3517.short: Nereus was a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.

G3518.name: Neri
G3518.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
G3518.short: Neri was an ancestor of Jesus, mentioned in Luke's genealogy.

G3505.name: Nero
G3505.desc: Emperor living at the time of the New Testament
G3505.short: Nero was likely the Roman emperor during Paul's final imprisonment.

G3527.name: Nicanor
G3527.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3527.short: Nicanor was one of the seven men chosen to assist the apostles in the early Jerusalem church.

G3530.name: Nicodemus
G3530.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3530.short: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council who had several encounters with Jesus.

G3532.name: Nicolaus
G3532.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3532.short: Nicolaus was a proselyte from Antioch chosen as one of the seven deacons in the early church.

G3564.name: Nympha
G3564.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G3564.brief: Hosted a church in her house
G3564.short: Nympha was a woman who hosted a church in her house in Laodicea.

G3533.name: Nicopolis
G3533.brief: A city in Epirus where Paul planned to winter
G3533.short: Nicopolis was a city in Epirus where Paul intended to spend the winter, as mentioned in his letter to Titus.

G3561.name: New Moon
G3561.brief: New Moon: A religious observance marking the beginning of months
G3561.short: The New Moon, mentioned in <ref="Col.2.16">Col.2.16</ref>, was a religious observance marking the beginning of each month in the Hebrew calendar, often celebrated with special sacrifices and feasts.

G3531.name: Nicolaitans
G3531.brief: A group whose practices were condemned by Jesus
G3531.short: The Nicolaitans, mentioned in <ref="Revelation 2:6; 2:15">Revelation 2:6; 2:15</ref>, were a group whose practices were hated by Jesus and condemned by the early church.
